notToBeConfusedWith.name: Bourbon
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Corn-forward and legally at least 51% corn in the mash; rye's mash is majority rye grain instead, which is where its drier, spicier profile comes from.

generalSubstitutes.note: Rounder and sweeter where rye is drier and spicier; a Manhattan made with it drinks softer and less peppery, with the vermouth reading sweeter against it.

forms.label: Standard strength
forms.sourceNote: Alcoholic beverage, distilled, whiskey, 86 proof. Public domain. USDA carries no record split out for rye specifically, so the same generic distilled-whiskey record used for this site's bourbon record is used here too. 86 US proof is 43% alcohol by volume by definition, close to the record's own measured ethanol-against-density figure of 42.9%. Standard ryes bottle from about 40% (Wild Turkey Rye) to 50% (Rittenhouse Bonded), and a bottle away from 43% moves every figure a drink using it computes. Gluten is not flagged: the spirit is distilled from grain and carries no protein through the still.
